title: Finite jets and graded algebra of a coefficient-extended power-series quotient
statement:
Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields, $e,s\geq0$, $R=K[[X_1,\ldots,X_e]]$, and $I\subseteq(X_1,\ldots,X_e)R$ an ideal. Put $C=R/I$, $D=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_e,T_1,\ldots,T_s]]/I L[[X,T]]$, $\mathfrak a=(X_1,\ldots,X_e)C$, and $\mathfrak b=(X_1,\ldots,X_e,T_1,\ldots,T_s)D$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The map $j:C\to D$ is induced by the specified coefficient inclusion and the $X$ variables. For $\beta\in\mathbf N^s$ write $|\beta|=\sum_i\beta_i$. For every $N\geq1$ the coefficient map gives an $L$-linear isomorphism
$$D/\mathfrak b^N\simeq\bigoplus_{|\beta|<N}\left(L\otimes_K(C/\mathfrak a^{N-|\beta|})\right)T^\beta$$
[def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. On truncated representatives it takes the coefficient of $T^\beta$ modulo $(X)^{N-|\beta|}+I$. Under these identifications reduction from $N+1$ to $N$ reduces every coefficient to the indicated smaller quotient and deletes the terms with $|\beta|=N$; products modulo $\mathfrak b^N$ are the coefficient-convolution products, with terms of $T$-degree at least $N$ discarded. In particular the homomorphism
$$\left(L\otimes_K\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak a}C\right)[T_1,\ldots,T_s]\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak b}D$$
[def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] sending $(\lambda\otimes[c])T^\beta$, for $c\in\mathfrak a^d$, to $[\lambda j(c)T^\beta]\in\mathfrak b^{d+|\beta|}/\mathfrak b^{d+|\beta|+1}$ is a graded $L$-algebra isomorphism. It uses the actual map $j$ on the constant-polynomial part. No finiteness assumption on $L/K$ is imposed.

proof.text: Write $S=L[[X,T]]$, $\mathfrak q=(X)R$, $\mathfrak v=(X,T)S$, and $E=IS$, the ideal of finite sums $\sum h_i f_i$ with $h_i\in S$, $f_i\in I$. The quotient maps give $C/\mathfrak a^m=R/(I+\mathfrak q^m)$ and $D/\mathfrak b^N=S/(E+\mathfrak v^N)$: products of image ideal generators generate the image ideal powers. Apply the cited coefficient criterion with base ideal zero. For positive $m,N$, $\mathfrak q^m$ and $\mathfrak v^N$ consist precisely of series with zero coefficients below the respective total-degree bounds. Thus their quotients have unique representatives supported below those bounds.

source.place: Agent application of lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients at base ideal zero; variable-power proof also read in literature/blueprint/latest/blueprint/sec-proper-base-change/sk-thm-p1/lem-weil-pbc-power-series-complete-over-complete-base.proof.md, paragraphs 1--3. No Stacks tag states this coefficient criterion.

proof.text: Let $W_m(K)$ be the space of polynomials in $X$ supported on $|\alpha|<m$, with multiplication followed by deletion of higher-degree terms; put $W_0(K)=0$, and similarly over $L$. Step 1 identifies $R/\mathfrak q^m=W_m(K)$. The coefficient map $L\otimes_K W_m(K)\to W_m(L)$ has inverse $\sum a_\alpha X^\alpha\mapsto\sum a_\alpha\otimes X^\alpha$. Tensor bilinearity proves that both composites are identities: on a pure tensor $\lambda\otimes\sum c_\alpha X^\alpha$, the inverse composite is $\sum\lambda c_\alpha\otimes X^\alpha=\lambda\otimes\sum c_\alpha X^\alpha$. The finite Cauchy product proves preservation of truncated multiplication. All these sums are finite, regardless of $[L:K]$.

source.place: Agent finite monomial coordinate calculation from the tensor universal property (Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product) and the power-series definition; no infinite tensor-product interchange.

proof.text: Let $U_m\subset W_m(K)$ be the image of $I$, with $U_0=0$. Grouping monomials of total degree below $N$ by their $T$ exponent gives $S/\mathfrak v^N=\bigoplus_{|\beta|<N}W_{N-|\beta|}(L)T^\beta$. The image of $E$ is exactly $\bigoplus_{|\beta|<N}\operatorname{im}(L\otimes_K U_{N-|\beta|})T^\beta$. Indeed, truncate a defining finite sum $\sum h_i f_i$ of $E$. Its $T^\beta$ coefficient modulo $(X)^{N-|\beta|}$ is a finite sum of terms $\lambda X^\alpha f_i$, with $\lambda\in L$ and $X^\alpha f_i\in I$, and hence lies in the indicated image. Conversely, each generator $\lambda\otimes u$ of this image has $u$ represented by some $f\in I$; the truncation of $\lambda fT^\beta\in E$ realizes that vector in just that summand. Finite sums prove the reverse inclusion.

source.place: Agent finite relation calculation for the algebraically extended ideal, using the finite Cauchy product and finite-sum definition of ideal extension.

proof.text: Reduction gives the exact sequence $U_m\to W_m(K)\to R/(I+\mathfrak q^m)\to0$. Tensor right exactness and step 2 identify $W_m(L)/\operatorname{im}(L\otimes_K U_m)$ with $L\otimes_K(C/\mathfrak a^m)$. Quotient the finite direct sum of step 3 componentwise: a tuple belongs to the relation subspace exactly when each component does. With step 1 this is the required $L$-linear finite-jet isomorphism. Its inverse sends $(\lambda\otimes[c])T^\beta$ to the class of $\lambda j(c)T^\beta$, choosing any lift of $c$ to $R$.

source.place: Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact), applied to the displayed relation-space sequence; explicit finite direct-sum quotient.

proof.text: Reduction from total cutoff $N+1$ to $N$ deletes exactly the monomials of degree $N$. In the $T^\beta$ component for $|\beta|<N$ it reduces the $X$ cutoff from $N+1-|\beta|$ to $N-|\beta|$; components with $|\beta|=N$ disappear. The images of $I$ reduce to the images of the same series of $I$. All maps in steps 2--4 use unchanged coefficients followed by these reductions, proving the asserted compatibility after quotienting by $E$.

source.place: Agent coefficient calculation comparing total cutoffs N+1 and N.

proof.text: For representatives $F=\sum_\beta f_\beta T^\beta$ and $G=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma T^\gamma$, the coefficient of $T^\delta$ in $FG$ is $\sum_{\beta+\gamma=\delta}f_\beta g_\gamma$ modulo $I+(X)^{N-|\delta|}$; terms with $|\delta|\ge N$ vanish. This is the defining Cauchy product. A change of $f_\beta$ by $I$ changes a product by $IS$. A change by $(X)^{N-|\beta|}$ changes its product with $g_\gamma T^\gamma$ by terms of total degree at least $N+|\gamma|\ge N$. Thus the formula descends to the tensor quotients. On pure tensors the coefficient product is $(\lambda\otimes[c])(\mu\otimes[d])=\lambda\mu\otimes[cd]$ at the required cutoff. This proves the product clause.

source.place: Agent Cauchy-product calculation; the product convention is the one in def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series.

proof.text: Fix $n\ge0$ and take the kernel of reduction from jet $n+1$ to jet $n$, with zeroth jet zero. On $D$ this kernel is $\mathfrak b^n/\mathfrak b^{n+1}$. The $K$-module $L$ is flat by the field-module lemma. Apply flat tensor exactness and tensor right exactness to $0\to\mathfrak a^d/\mathfrak a^{d+1}\to C/\mathfrak a^{d+1}\to C/\mathfrak a^d\to0$. In the $\beta$ component for $|\beta|\le n$, set $d=n-|\beta|$. Its kernel is $L\otimes_K(\mathfrak a^d/\mathfrak a^{d+1})$. This also covers $|\beta|=n$: then $d=0$ and $C/\mathfrak a^0=0$. Step 5 gives a bijection $\bigoplus_{|\beta|\le n}\left(L\otimes_K(\mathfrak a^{n-|\beta|}/\mathfrak a^{n+1-|\beta|})\right)T^\beta\simeq\mathfrak b^n/\mathfrak b^{n+1}$, sending $\lambda\otimes[c]$ to $[\lambda j(c)T^\beta]$.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat) and Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact), applied to the displayed successive-power short exact sequence; field flatness from the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: The degree-$n$ part of $(L\otimes_K\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak a}C)[T]$ is the direct sum in step 7. To check this directly, expand each polynomial into its finitely many $T$ monomials and each tensor coefficient into its finitely many graded components. The maps $\lambda\otimes\sum_d c_d\mapsto\sum_d\lambda\otimes c_d$ and insertion of components are inverse by bilinearity and finite support. Reindex the finite pairs $(d,\beta)$ by $n=d+|\beta|$. Taking the direct sum of step 7 therefore gives a bijective graded $L$-linear map with precisely the formula in the statement.

source.place: Agent explicit finite-support reindexing of tensor, graded and polynomial components.

proof.text: For $c\in\mathfrak a^d$ and $c'\in\mathfrak a^{d'}$, the product of their images is $[\lambda j(c)T^\beta][\mu j(c')T^\gamma]=[\lambda\mu j(cc')T^{\beta+\gamma}]$ in degree $d+d'+|\beta|+|\gamma|$. The cited associated-graded structure gives exactly this representative product rule. It is the image of the product of the homogeneous pure tensors, so finite additivity proves multiplicativity everywhere. Unit and $L$-scalars go to their own degree-zero classes. Thus the bijection is a graded $L$-algebra isomorphism. For $\beta=0$ its formula is $\lambda\otimes[c]\mapsto[\lambda j(c)]$, verifying the actual map $j$ on the constant-polynomial part.
